title: dwo-extreme
label: Switchblade

won.source: The fed's own Champions page: "Extreme Championship / Switchblade / Won- 5.23.02" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-champions-2002-06.html).

how: The fed's own Champions page records the date and nothing about the match.
note: Defended it three weeks later against Jonan in an extreme glass hands match, both men's hands taped and doused in glass, on the fed's own Travesty card of 13 June 2002.

title: dwo-extreme
label: Kuff McSlade

won.source: The fed's own Travesty of 10 July 2003, whose commentary places the win "the week after" and whose main event he wins as "STILL DWO EXTREME CHAMPION" (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-07-10.html).

how: Retained against the returning Tyrone Grace in the main event of 10 July 2003, and was welcomed into the DoD by the man he beat afterwards.
note: The match in which he won the belt is not held. By the fed's own Relentless of 25 September 2003 the Extreme Championship is on Sean Quinn.

title: dwo-heavyweight
label: John Miro

won.source: The fed's own Champions page: "Heavyweight Championship / John Miro / Won- 4.21.02" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-champions-2002-06.html).

how: The fed's own Champions page records the date and nothing about the match.
note: Still listed as champion on the 8 June 2002 capture of that page, with Lethal named as his number one contender.

title: dwo-heavyweight
label: AJ Trinidad

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — the fed's own news item of 10 June 2002 reaches him already champion ("Our heavyweight champion, AJ Trinidad", /promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-news-2002-05-to-06.html).

how: Not recovered. The Champions page still had John Miro on 8 June 2002 and the newsdesk had Trinidad on 10 June; no document held covers the change.
note: Still champion on 22 August 2002, when Mike Pizaz beat him in a non-title match on his own debut, and still defending it against Jackson Rust at the fed's own Blackshock afterwards.

title: dwo-heavyweight
label: Jackson Rust

won.source: The fed's own Travesty main event of October 2002, in which he is announced as "your winner and STILL DWO WORLD CHAMPION" after retaining against Adam Stryker (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2002-10-main-event.html).

how: Not recovered — the record reaches him already champion and watches him retain in an anything-goes match against Adam Stryker.
note: Chryste's own dialogue that autumn calls him "our best at the time". The belt is vacant by December, when the fed runs a World Title tournament to fill it; nothing held records how his reign ended.

title: dwo-heavyweight
label: Adam Stryker

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — the fed's own post-pay-per-view Travesty segment of 4 October 2002 has him carrying the belt and calling himself "Current WORLD Champion" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-news-2002-09-to-10.html).

how: Not recovered. The fed's own October 2002 main-event commentary refers back to "Stryker's last and only World Title match against AJ Trinidad".
note: SOURCES DISAGREE. The same fortnight has Adam Stryker carrying the World Title in one served segment and Jackson Rust defending it against him in another. Both are recorded; neither is picked, and no document held dates a change between them.

title: dwo-heavyweight
label: Kaiowas

won.source: The fed's own Christmas Chaos report: the World Title Tourney came down to Kaiowas against Julius Corbin, "to determine the new DWO World Champion, to be crowned at the next Travesty" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-news-2002-12-to-2003-01.html); the fed's own news of 25 January 2003 calls him "our current DWO Heavyweight Champion".

how: Won the final of the DWO World Title tournament against Julius Corbin, at the Travesty following Christmas Chaos. He had beaten The Event and then Vash to reach it.
note: The tournament ran through December 2002 to fill the belt after Lexis Bane's own shutdown of the fed. He was booked to defend it against Rainer inside the Crimson Steel Cage at Lord of the Asylum: Crimson Dance on 31 January 2003; no account of that match survives.

title: dwo-heavyweight
label: Donny Diamond

won.source: Primetime Central's own New Era results, which stage the DWO World Heavyweight Title match on the alliance's own supercard and record Kaiowas losing it (/promotions/ptc/archive/new-era-2003-results.html).

how: def. Kaiowas (c) in the DWO Asylum, on Primetime Central's own New Era interfed supercard. He won the PTC Global Championship later the same night.
note: The only DWO title change anywhere in the record that is dated to the day, and the receipt for it is another promotion's. The show is Primetime Central's own canonical row; this reign references it rather than duplicating it. RESOLVED FURTHER: the reign ended in-fiction by Donny Diamond's own kayfabe death, revealed on the fed's own Travesty of 10 July 2003 — Damian and Samantha claim to have killed him at an LOA event the week before, taking his own pentagram necklace as a trophy and relaunching the Disciples of Darkness in his place. No card carrying the killing itself is held; see dwo-loa-donny-diamond-death-2003-07 (collected: false).

end.source: The fed's own Travesty of 10 July 2003 has Damian and Samantha reveal they killed Donny Diamond at a Lord of the Asylum event "the week before" (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-07-10.html).

title: dwo-heavyweight
label: Kaiowas

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — the fed's own Travesty of 10 July 2003 has its commentary call him "the DWO World Champion" in the middle of the non-title match he loses to Kai Shinobi (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-07-10.html).

how: Not recovered. The record has him lose the belt on 20 April 2003 and hold it again by 10 July, with nothing held in between.
note: A second reign, recorded because the fed's own commentary states it plainly; how and when he regained the title is not in anything held. Donny Diamond's own reign is now known to have ended in his own kayfabe death rather than a lost match — see that row's own note — which explains why the belt was open, though not how or when Kaiowas specifically regained it. SOURCES DISAGREE, RECORDED HONESTLY: by 25 September 2003 Callisto Bane calls Donny Diamond the reigning Heavyweight Champion, meaning the belt changed hands from Kaiowas a second time — undated, unwitnessed in anything held, and never reconciled anywhere held with Damian and Samantha's own claim five weeks earlier to have killed Donny Diamond (dwo-travesty-2003-07-10). Recorded as a new reign rather than picked apart or resolved by guess.

end.source: Relentless, 25 September 2003, has Callisto Bane call Donny Diamond the reigning Heavyweight Champion, booking Damian against him for the belt at the coming pay-per-view (/promotions/dwo/archive/relentless-2003-09-25.html).

title: dwo-intercontinental
label: Angelus

won.source: The fed's own Champions page: "Intercontiental Championship / Angelus / Won- 3.25.02" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-champions-2002-06.html).

how: The fed's own Champions page records the date and nothing about the match. This is the earliest dated title reign anywhere in the DWO's own record.
note: Still champion on the 8 June 2002 capture of that page, with the contendership listed TBA.

title: dwo-pride
label: Regin

won.source: The fed's own Travesty card of 9 October 2003, which has "the current Pride Champion commentating" on the challenger's match and names him Regin (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-10-09-card.html).

note: The belt itself first appears in the held record on 10 July 2003, when the fed runs a number one contender's match for it.

title: dwo-rising-dominance
label: Carys

won.source: The fed's own Travesty of 22 May 2003, which previews "the RD Title match, pitting Carys against" a challenger for "her title" (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-05-22.html).

how: Not recovered. The fed ran brackets for the belt through April 2003; the second set, naming the last two competitors, ran on Travesty of 11 April.

title: dwo-rising-dominance
label: Angelus Sorrow

won.source: Undated. The claim is his own Lights Out Wrestling bio card, which lists among his other-federation awards “DWO Rising Dominance Champion (last ever)” (promotions/low/archive/angelus-sorrow-bio-card.html, captured 8 July 2004).

note: THE ONLY ACCOUNT ANYWHERE OF HOW A DWO TITLE ENDED, AND IT COMES FROM OUTSIDE THE FED. No DWO document records this reign — the fed's own 2003 title page (champs1.htm) was never captured. What DOES corroborate the man's presence in the DWO is the fed's own UnStAbLe prediction poll of October 2002, which has “Match Four: Sorrow 9 / Frost 2” (/promotions/dwo/archive/loa-unstable-predictions-2002.html). The “last ever” wording is a wrestler's own self-reported honour on a bio card at another federation, not a ledger, and is recorded as exactly that.

title: dwo-tag-team
label: Gina and Angelus

won.source: The fed's own Champions page: "Tag Team Championships / Gina and Angelus / Won- 5.16.02" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-champions-2002-06.html).

how: The fed's own Champions page records the date and nothing about the match.
note: Defended on the fed's own Travesty card of 13 June 2002 against Adam Stryker and Sean Campbell; Shock Syndrome then ran a number one contendership tag elimination for the belts that ended in a no contest.

title: dwo-tag-team
label: Chryste and Carys

won.source: The fed's own Travesty of 22 May 2003, whose commentary names Tyrone Grace as the man "who lost the Tag Titles to Chryste and Carys" (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-05-22.html).

how: Taken off Tyrone Grace's side; the match itself is not held.
note: By the fed's own card of 9 October 2003 the belts are on Damian and Roulette, defending against Hecate and Arsenic. Draven's own tag reign at UnStAbLe in September 2002 sits between this and the fed's first recorded champions, and no date for it survives.

how: The fed's own Champions page records the date and nothing about the match.
note: Ended in the three-way ladder finish at Shock Syndrome that the fed's own results page scored "Winner by ?: Kristi Kiss.. Lana Day.. Jaslene Myst...", and that its own newsdesk reported as three women all holding a claim to the belt with the officials stumped. Nothing held records a resolution.

title: dwo-heavyweight
label: Donny Diamond

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — Relentless, 25 September 2003, has Callisto Bane call him the reigning Heavyweight Champion and book Damian against him for the belt at the coming pay-per-view (/promotions/dwo/archive/relentless-2003-09-25.html).

how: Not recovered. Regained the title from Kaiowas (dwo-heavyweight-r007) at some point between 10 July and 25 September 2003, with nothing held documenting the change.
note: A second reign, recorded because the fed's own commentary states it plainly. It is never reconciled anywhere held with Damian and Samantha's own claim five weeks earlier (dwo-travesty-2003-07-10) to have killed Donny Diamond — the museum records what each document says and picks no side. He is billed to defend against Damian at the coming pay-per-view, Lord of the Asylum: Descent into Darkness (dwo-descent-into-darkness-2003-09, collected: false); no result for that show survives.

title: dwo-extreme
label: Sean Quinn

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — Relentless, 25 September 2003, has Jay call it "Sean Quinn's Extreme title" ahead of a since-cancelled main event, and Callisto Bane books it against the vacated Intercontinental title at the coming pay-per-view (/promotions/dwo/archive/relentless-2003-09-25.html).

how: Not recovered. Took the belt from Kuff McSlade (dwo-extreme-r002) at some point between 10 July and 25 September 2003.
note: Booked to defend it against Tyrone Grace at Lord of the Asylum: Descent into Darkness (dwo-descent-into-darkness-2003-09, collected: false), where the vacated Intercontinental title is also on the line — "first and second pin get different titles." No result for that show survives.

title: dwo-intercontinental
label: Damian

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — Relentless, 25 September 2003, has Callisto Bane and the fed's own commentary treat Damian as the reigning Intercontinental Champion before forcing him to vacate it (/promotions/dwo/archive/relentless-2003-09-25.html).

how: Won from someone unrecorded, at some point after Angelus's own reign (dwo-intercontinental-r001, last attested June 2002). Vacated on Callisto Bane's own order on Relentless, 25 September 2003, in exchange for a Heavyweight title shot against Donny Diamond at the coming pay-per-view.
note: Fifteen months separate this reign from Angelus's own — nothing held names an intervening champion, if there was one. The vacated belt is booked into a winner-take-one match between Tyrone Grace and Sean Quinn at Lord of the Asylum: Descent into Darkness (dwo-descent-into-darkness-2003-09, collected: false); no result for that show survives.
